answer: Trust propagates from honest seeds through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, making influence depend on verified connectivity rather than self-created identities. A sybil cluster usually connects through a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits probability mass crossing into the cluster, while min-cut transitivity bounds the total voting weight that mutually reinforcing nodes can accumulate. Thus timber, garden, and ripple identities cannot amplify one another beyond the cut’s capacity.
